sources.note: Hybrid+EV filter returned 37 listings across 2 pages; a second model-filtered efficient-gas pass (21 exemplar models) returned 226 listings across 10 pages. Detail pages remain bot-blocked, so VIN/title/accident are missing for Cars.com rows. Most Cars.com cars were also on CarGurus with richer data and were deduped there.

Hybrid+Electric fuel filter (105 listings, 5 pages) plus a gasoline pass with the site's own minMpg=32 filter (178 listings, 9 pages). Best source for deal ratings, price-vs-market deltas, VINs and days-on-market. Note: prices captured as all-in totalPrice, not the pre-fee base price.

23 model queries against the Denver cta board (hybrid, prius, leaf, ct200h, niro, ioniq, insight, volt, c-max, energi, camry/sonata hybrid, plus the efficient-gas models). A large share of the cheap dealer posts are payment-teaser bait (2024 Sentra at $6,450, 2019 Corolla XLE at $5,950 from one Morrison Rd address) and were screened out.

Dropped minPrice/sortBy (they wedge the grid) and ran 14 queries with lazy-load scrolling: hybrid, prius, nissan leaf, chevy volt, camry hybrid, fusion hybrid, kia niro, lexus ct, toyota corolla, honda civic, honda fit, hyundai elantra, nissan sentra, mazda 3. Opened 10 detail pages for mileage/title/photos. Several dealer cross-posts were deduped against CarGurus.
Price filter URLs redirect to the homepage; sorted the national list by price instead - cheapest real vehicle is $16,990 and their lowest marketing tier is 'Cars under $20K'. Nothing under $10,000.

First attempt with the 100-mile radius params hit a bot challenge; retried without them and the search loaded (61 Buy-It-Now cars under $10k). None showed a Colorado location - eBay reports these as 'Located in United States' - so nothing was verifiably local.

Ran prius, nissan leaf, toyota corolla, honda civic and hybrid queries. Only the Aurora 2016 Prius c cleared the bar; the Civics found here were higher-mileage than the CarGurus equivalents and the 2012 Leaf was the same AutoNation car already captured.
The fuel-filter URL 404s; used their own search sorted by price ascending within 100 miles of 80015 (1,581 vehicles). Cheapest unit is $15,560. Nothing under $10,000.

The documented search URL 404s now; used /search sorted price-ascending for zip 80015 with no fuel restriction (10,000 results). Cheapest unit is $16,698, and their lowest price band starts at 'Under $20k'. Nothing under $10,000.
Deliberately not searched - 27 qualifying candidates were found inside the 100-mile radius, so there was no reason to stretch to Utah (350+ miles) this run.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatchback with an upright rear bench and a high roofline - one of the easiest cars here to lift a child into, and the hatch swallows a stroller plus daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Private seller in Colorado Springs - message for the VIN and a photo of the title, then run a history report BEFORE committing to the 54-mile drive. Ask whether the 2013 C-Max recall work (8 open campaigns for this model year) was completed.
listings.why: Best miles-per-dollar hybrid found this run: 79k miles for $6,200 with a seller-stated clean title and no damage, at 40 mpg combined. Roughly 45,000 fewer miles than the Centennial Fusion Hybrid for $1,200 less. The 54-mile drive and the long 2013 Ford recall list are the trade-offs.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - the easiest shape here for a rear-facing seat. Deep rear footwell, full-size door opening, and a big trunk for the daycare run.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 5 miles away - request the free Carfax link and receipts for the hybrid battery cooling filter, then book a pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: 41 mpg in a 5-star midsize sedan, clean title, zero accidents, $1,567 under CarGurus market and the closest family-shaped hybrid to home. Only 1 open recall campaign for the model year.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Same tall-hatch shape as the number-one pick but four model years newer - upright rear seat, easy child-seat access, generous hatch space.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - one accident on record, so ask for the Carfax damage detail and have the rear structure inspected. It has sat 58 days, so there is room to negotiate.
listings.why: Biggest below-market delta of any hybrid on the board (-$2,846), 40 mpg, only 85k miles on a 2017, clean title and just one open recall. The single accident report is the only real caveat.

listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover-height hatchback: the high hip point makes buckling a child seat much easier on your back, and the cargo area takes a stroller upright.
listings.nextAction: Small Aurora dealer (RNBCARS INC, 11111 E Mississippi Ave) - ask for the VIN and Carfax, confirm the charge port works and the ~26-mile electric range still holds, and check whether Kia's 10-year/100k battery warranty transfers.
listings.why: Newest car on the entire board and the only plug-in under $10k that is 5 minutes from home. Its 26 electric miles cover the whole Lone Tree + daycare loop on Level 1 charging, and it falls back to 46 mpg on gas for road trips.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat - the most rear-facing clearance of anything on this list, with a flat floor if a second adult ever rides in back.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 3 open recall campaigns plus 1 accident reported; ask for recall completion receipts and the Carfax damage detail before you make an offer.
listings.why: Biggest cabin on the board at 40 mpg, 5-star NHTSA overall, $1,709 under market, and Hyundai's 10-year hybrid battery coverage is the longest in the segment.

listings.carSeatNotes: The Fit's Magic Seat and tall roofline give it more usable rear space than cars a class above; wide rear doors and a low load floor make the car seat easy to fit.
listings.nextAction: Just-listed dealer car 9 miles away - request the free Carfax and confirm the four open recalls (Takata-era airbag work) were completed. Verify it is the CVT, not the manual, since the manual only rates 32 mpg.
listings.why: 36 mpg combined from a pure-gas car with 5-star NHTSA safety and Honda drivetrain durability, $2,207 under market. The most practical non-hybrid shape here for daycare gear.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Rear seat is tight and the 2011-2015 Volt has a two-seat rear bench split by a center console - fine for one child seat, awkward if another passenger rides back there.
listings.nextAction: Private seller says clean CO title in hand, fresh winter tires and a new aux battery, but it needs an alignment and oil change - price that in. Ask for a dash photo showing current electric range before driving to Golden.
listings.why: 38 electric miles covers your whole workday loop on Level 1 charging, with a gas engine for trips. 5-star NHTSA, lowest miles of any Volt found, and the seller has already done the winter tires.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a genuinely roomy rear bench and easy-to-reach lower LATCH anchors; a rear-facing seat fits without pushing the front passenger far forward.
listings.nextAction: Listed today at an EchoPark store 6 miles away - request the Carfax and, most important, confirm the CVT has service records. That transmission is this car's known weak point.
listings.why: Replaces yesterday's Littleton Sentra (which sold): 79,589 miles for $7,997, $1,602 under market, six miles from home. Cheap to run and cheap to fix, and it just clears the 32 mpg floor.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan - a rear-facing seat fits but front-passenger legroom gets tight. Test-fit your actual seat. Standard low-speed automatic emergency braking is a real safety bonus at this price.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - zero open recalls, so put the money into a pre-purchase inspection instead and ask for the Carfax.
listings.why: 36 mpg, zero open recalls, Mazda2 mechanics under Toyota's warranty pedigree, and it came standard with automatic emergency braking - almost unheard of under $10k. $1,976 under market.

listings.carSeatNotes: Rear seat is a little snug front-to-back for rear-facing; test-fit before buying. The doors open wide and the seat backs are upright, which helps.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 8 miles away - 4 open recall campaigns for this model year, so ask for completion receipts plus the Carfax.
listings.why: $1,049 cheaper than yesterday's 2016 Mazda3 for similar miles. 5-star safety, 33 mpg, and this generation of Mazda3 ages unusually well mechanically.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same roomy Sentra rear bench; the 2019 SV adds standard forward-collision warning and automatic emergency braking - the best active-safety kit of any gas car here.
listings.nextAction: Dealer in Aurora, 5 miles away - request the Carfax and CVT service history. At 111k miles the transmission record matters more than anything else on this car.
listings.why: $1,442 cheaper than the other 2019 Sentra SV on the board and 5 minutes from home, with standard automatic emergency braking and $1,912 under market. Mileage is the trade-off.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover ride height makes loading a child seat much easier on your back, and the hatch area holds a stroller upright.
listings.nextAction: Private seller in Aurora, 2 owners, states clean Colorado title and no damage. Make any offer contingent on a hybrid-system scan and dual-clutch transmission service records given the 142k miles.
listings.why: 49 mpg combined - the highest-mpg non-plug-in on the board - in the most family-friendly body style, 5 minutes from home, with a stated clean title. High mileage is the reason it is not higher.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Same tight four-seat Volt cabin - workable for one rear-facing seat, but verify front-passenger legroom with the seat installed.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 5 miles away - ask for the battery state-of-health readout and confirm the 8-year/100k battery warranty has not just expired on mileage (it is at 100,289).
listings.why: Dealer-backed Volt with a clean title and zero accidents, 5 miles from home. $749 more than the Golden private-party car for materially less risk.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a flat, wide rear bench and a good door aperture - a rear-facing seat goes in easily and the hatch holds daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Ask the dealer to photograph the dash battery-capacity bars (12 = healthy) or run a LeafSpy report before you drive out.
listings.why: 2017 is the first Leaf year worth buying (30 kWh, ~107 miles new). Even at 70% health that is ~75 miles - triple your 25-mile workday - and a regular outlet refills it overnight. Colorado winter will cut range 20-30%, which still leaves plenty of margin.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - a rear-facing seat will fit but expect to slide the front passenger seat well forward. Test-fit your actual seat before buying.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - one accident reported and no title status shown; ask for the Carfax and confirm the title is clean before you go look at it.
listings.why: Cheapest 50-mpg car in the metro, and Toyota hybrid reliability is the safest bet in this segment. Docked for interior size and the accident report.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat with excellent rear-facing clearance; the trunk is reduced by the battery but still holds a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - ask whether the 10-year/100k plug-in battery warranty transferred, and confirm the charge port and the ~29-mile range still work.
listings.why: Largest plug-in here: 29 electric miles covers most of your daily loop, 5-star NHTSA, midsize cabin, $1,467 under market. 127k miles on a PHEV is the main risk.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatch with an upright rear seat - very easy child-seat access, though the Energi battery raises the cargo floor.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 8 recall campaigns exist for this model year; ask for completion receipts, and verify the plug-in battery still holds its ~21-mile range.
listings.why: Lowest mileage on the entire board (51,856) and a plug-in that would cover most of your daily loop on electricity. Priced at the top of budget and it is a 54-mile drive.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan - rear-facing fits but front-passenger legroom gets tight. Standard low-speed automatic emergency braking is a genuine plus for a family car.
listings.nextAction: It has been listed 116 days without selling, so open below asking. Zero open recalls - spend the money on a pre-purchase inspection and ask for the Carfax.
listings.why: Lowest-mileage gas car found (51,786), 5-star NHTSA, 35 mpg, zero open recalls, and it is the same Mazda2-based car as the Scion iA but two model years newer. Top of budget and small inside.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover-height hatchback: high hip point makes buckling a child seat much easier, and the cargo area handles a stroller upright.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - at 157k miles make the deal contingent on a hybrid-system scan and ask for dual-clutch transmission service records.
listings.why: Dealer-backed alternative to the private Aurora Niro: clean title, zero accidents, $644 under market - but 15,000 more miles for $102 less. Take whichever inspects better.

listings.carSeatNotes: Easy hatchback child-seat access, but the small cabin plus limited range makes this a second car rather than the family car.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery report before anything else - a 2012 Leaf with a weak pack is worth far less than the asking price. Also cross-listed on Cars.com and OfferUp by the same AutoNation store.
listings.why: Cheapest EV on the board, zero open recalls, mechanically about as simple as a car gets. But a 2012 24 kWh pack is likely down to 40-55 real miles, and Colorado winter cuts that further.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy compact rear seat with a wide door opening; the hatchback version swallows a stroller. All-wheel drive is the practical safety story for Colorado winters.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 7 open recall campaigns for this model year, so ask for completion receipts, and get the CVT inspected before committing.
listings.why: The only AWD car that clears the 32 mpg floor: 5-star NHTSA, $1,950 under market, and genuinely useful in Denver snow. It will cost a bit more to maintain than a Corolla.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy compact rear bench with accessible LATCH anchors; rear-facing fits without crowding the driver.
listings.nextAction: Cheapest usable car on the list, listed 49 days - open below asking. Insist on CVT service records and a pre-purchase inspection; 5 open recalls need completion receipts.
listings.why: $5,287 for a 33-mpg compact that is $1,854 under market leaves a lot of budget for a proper inspection and any deferred maintenance. Also cross-listed on Cars.com.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomiest rear seat of any car on this list and a full-size trunk - the easiest daily child-seat car here.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 4 miles away, listed since early May - there is real room to negotiate. Ask for the Carfax and a hybrid battery health check. Also cross-posted on Facebook Marketplace by the same dealer.
listings.why: Toyota hybrid reliability in a midsize body 4 miles from home, 40 mpg, 5-star safety. Priced at the very top of budget, but 109 days unsold is leverage.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - test-fit your rear-facing seat before committing; front-passenger legroom is the constraint.
listings.nextAction: Listed since mid-July with no price movement - message with a below-ask offer and request the VIN and a photo of the title.
listings.why: Zero open recalls, 50 mpg, and it is in Aurora, five minutes away. A stale listing means real negotiating room. Interior size is the only real knock.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize rear seat with plenty of rear-facing clearance and a large trunk.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - the 2011-2014 Sonata Hybrid used a lithium-polymer pack with a mixed reliability record. Ask for the VIN and any battery or engine replacement receipts before viewing.
listings.why: 82,500 miles for $7,000 in a 5-star midsize hybrid is strong money, but this generation's hybrid system and 2.4L engine are the least proven on this list. Inspect carefully.

listings.carSeatNotes: Best-in-class rear legroom for a compact - rear-facing goes in with room to spare and the doors open nearly square.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before driving to Todd Creek, and get a pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: Low-mileage 5-star Corolla with the most bulletproof drivetrain on this list. Priced near the top of budget for what it is, which is why it sits here rather than higher.

listings.accident: Seller states significant body damage from an uninsured collision
listings.carSeatNotes: The Corolla rear seat is one of the roomiest in the compact class - but crash-damaged structure is exactly the wrong thing to put a child seat into until it is properly repaired and inspected.
listings.nextAction: DOWNGRADED - reading the full listing today, the seller writes that the car was in an accident with significant body damage and no collision coverage, and offers a repair estimate. Do not buy this without an independent body-shop assessment of frame and structural damage plus the repair cost. Assume the real all-in price is well above $6,500.
listings.why: Ranked #2 yesterday on the headline numbers - 34 mpg, 5-star, cheap - but the seller's own description discloses unrepaired collision damage. Kept on the board only so the change is visible; treat as a project car, not a family car.
